title: Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (YGTSS): Psychometric Quality of the Gold Standard for Tic Assessment Based on the Large-Scale EMTICS Study
evidence_type: Peer-reviewed cross-sectional psychometric analysis of longitudinal cohort baseline
review_scope: Historical source selected by October 26 research plan, not new-window discovery
population: Children ages 3–16 in 16 European clinical centers; original YGTSS, not administered YGTSS-R validation
eligibility: Linked protocol PMID 29982875 permits ASD but excludes inability of child to understand/comply or parental inability to comply; eligibility does not establish ASD representation or subgroup validity. Serious medical/neurological illness and recent antibiotics also excluded in protocol.
comparator: CGI-S for convergence; CY-BOCS, parent SNAP-IV and SDQ internalizing for discrimination; ordinal two-factor model and coefficient comparison
outcomes: Original YGTSS total tic score (TTS), separately rated impairment and global sum (GSS), not all lived burden
follow_up: Baseline only for this analysis, not longitudinal response or prediction
uncertainty: Exact omega variant, formula and implementation not verified in main report or inspected supplement; no coefficient uncertainty or new estimates reconstructed. Good alpha does not imply good fit, omega is not treated as true reliability.
negative_and_conflicting_evidence: Marginal factor fit and at least 13 residual-error misspecifications; subsequent EFA no satisfactory alternative
Supplement has 13 misspecification and two inconclusive rows; omitted no-misspecification rows and mixed expected parameter change signs retained
No empirical interrater reliability or language-stratified validation
No adult or ASD/communication-group measurement equivalence demonstrated
Methods ≥8 versus Results >8 subgroup wording discrepancy retained
Past-week modality absence counts use full 706 denominator, not 624 TS denominator
Abstract OCD correlation appears as 27; explicit Table 2 value .27 extracted
attrition_missingness: 706 retained after baseline cleaning/eligibility; pair-specific correlation counts and complete missingness handling not established in inspected report
adverse_events: Not intervention safety research; no absence-of-risk inference
risk_of_bias: Clinic-based pediatric cohort with relatively low average impairment
Mixed languages and centers without language-specific validation
Only CGI-S convergence comparator; independent blinding not established
Small chronic-vocal subgroup; no severe-adult representation
funding_conflicts: EMTICS European research funding; author disclosures include multiple institutional and industry research/consultancy relationships; not conflict-free certification
claim_supported: Convergence/discrimination evidence coexists with limited factorial fit, coefficient dependence and reasons to keep tic severity and impairment distinct
claim_not_supported: Omega is true reliability or alpha bias equals coefficient gap
Treatment response, remission or causal mechanism
retrieval_status: Publisher full HTML and official EuropePMC XML inspected transiently; independent reviewer retrieved official supplemental aggregate table and visually checked it. Direct PMC challenged. No full-text or participant files retained.
correction_retraction_check: No PubMed linked notice or notice in bounded exact-DOI search; not comprehensive clearance
reviewer: AI-assisted source/methods audit with independent source/arithmetic review; not clinical peer review
computation: Deterministic coefficient-gap and published-cutoff sensitivity on rounded aggregates; no model fitting or simulation
next_verification_task: Bounded Ho et al. 2020 parent-versus-clinician audit (PMID 32819930, DOI 10.1136/bmjopen-2019-034634): agreement vs correlation, repeated-visit unit, informant independence, completeness/version and subgroup eligibility; no extrapolation to adult/ASD.
